text: Git branching is an essential feature of version control that allows developers to work on different parts of a project simultaneously. Instead of modifying the main code directly, programmers create separate feature branches to develop new functionality or fix bugs. Each branch operates independently, giving developers the freedom to experiment without risk. Once work on a feature branch is complete, it can be integrated through merging back into the main branch. In team workflows, this process is often managed with pull requests, which let other team members review the code changes before they are accepted. This structured version control workflow ensures that the main project remains stable and reliable at all times.
